description: The convention-C H_3 Gram determinant's recorded factorisation is explained: det G = [unit on u>0] * y_(3) * y_(2,1)^4 * y_(1^3), so every positive-u degeneracy is a Wedderburn weight vanishing and the multiplicity-5 factors are d^2 bookkeeping. y_(2,1) = 0 iff z = q or z = -1/q; under convention C those are exactly detFactor3 (u^3+u-1) and detFactor4 (u^3+u^2+1). Under the canonical convention D neither has a real solution and y_(2,1)(z_D) = q^2/(q^2+1)^2 > 0, so the hadronic-melt degeneracy does not exist at any real q. Separately, spectrahedral-phase-collapse-melt.md misplaces the convention-C threshold (it says q = psi; the theorem gives u = 1/psi with u = sqrt(q), i.e. q = 1/psi^2) and inverts its direction (it says heated past; the weight goes negative BELOW).

data.scope: Scope-(b) for 'the (2,1) Wedderburn weight cannot vanish at any real q under convention D', with the invariant cited: y_(2,1)(z_D) = q^2/(q^2+1)^2 is a manifestly positive rational function. Scope-(a) for 'there is no hadronic melt' — this excludes the Wedderburn / Gram-degeneracy route only; a transition from some other mechanism is untouched.
